The claim for compensation raised in the present Detailed Accident Report (DAR) is in respect of fatal injuries alleged to have been sustained by the deceased Sh. Manpreet Singh in a motor accident that took place on 12.03.2016 at about 9:07 pm at NH-8, Main Road near Landing Point,
Mahipalpur, New Delhi, regarding which one FIR No.173/2016, under Sections 279/337 IPC was Jagjeet Singh vs Chandan on 8 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62281313/
1 registered at PS Vasant Kunj North.
Later offence punishable under Section 304-A IPC was added.

The vehicle involved in this case is Champion (three wheeler) bearing registration No.
DL-1LL-8924, which at the relevant time of accident was being driven by respondent no.1 Sh.
Chandan (R1) and owned by respondent no. 2 Sh. Satpal (R2).
2.
The peculiar facts of the case as disclosed in the DAR are that a PCR call was received on 12.03.2016 at 09:07 PM from one Ankit whose statement was recorded later by the IO.
Sh. Ankit informed that their vehicle Champion had got punctured.
At that time, hail storm was going on and it was raining also.
Because of this, they were seated in the vehicle.
Suddenly, a scooty fell down in front of the said vehicle and a Sikh person driving the scooty also fell down.
The caller further informed that it appeared as if some one had hit the scooty because of which the scooty fell in front of Champion vehicle.
Because of rain and hail, caller could not see how the accident took place.
After the PCR van took the injured away, the caller also left with his vehicle.
From the statement of the caller in Hindi recorded by the police, it is apparent that more than one person were sitting the said vehicle.
As per the DAR/chargesheet, Sh. Ankit was sitting in the Champion vehicle as a helper along with driver (R-1) Sh. Chandan.
Father of the injured informed the IO that his son Manpreet (deceased) worked in a private company in Gurgaon and was on his way to his night shift when the accident took place.
In his statement, he further informed that he had talked to the caller but he was not able to give registration no. of any vehicle.

3. Thereafter, on 17.09.2016, Claimant Sh. Jagjeet Singh (father of the deceased) informed that one Sh. Ajeet Singh who was present at the spot on the time of accident had informed him that one goods carrying auto bearing registration no. DL-1LL-8924 had hit his son's scooty and then fled from the spot.

4. Chargesheet further shows that a notice u/s 133 MV Act was issued against Sh. Satpal, the registered owner of the offending vehicle, who produced the said vehicle before the IO along with driver Chandan.
It has been endorsed on the notice u/s 133 MV Act by Sh. Satpal that the offending vehicle was being driven by R-1 Sh. Chandan on 22.02.2017 and that Sh. Chandan had informed him about the accident.

5. Accordingly, after conclusion of investigation, chargesheet for the offences punishable u/s 279/338/304A IPC (against R-1 Sh. Chandan) and u/s 420 IPC and 146/196 MV Act (against R-2/registered owner Sh. Satpal on account of fake insurance policy) was filed.

6. Respondent nos.1 and 2 have filed their reply to the DAR wherein they claimed to be the good samaritans and submitted that the helper Sh. Ankit had informed the police about the accident and had also called the ambulance.

Sh. Ankit was sitting in the offending vehicle along with driver Sh.
Chandan at that time.
It is submitted that there is an inordinate delay in registration of FIR.
It is further submitted that the owner of the offending vehicle had been cheated by the Insurance Agent.
The details of the fake insurance policies issued by that insurance agent have also been enumerated by the respondents.
It is submitted that possibility of occurrence of accident because of slippery road cannot be ruled out.

On 16.01.2018, the following issues were framed by this tribunal as:-
1.

Whether the deceased Manpreet Singh sustained fatal injuries in the accident which occurred on 12.03.2016 at about 09.07 PM at NH-8, Main Road Near Landing Point Mahipalpur, New Delhi caused by rash and negligent driving of vehicle No.
DL-1LL-8924 being driven by respondent no. 1 and owned by respondent no. 2 ?

OPP.
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, to what amount and from whom?

OPP 3. Relief.

The findings on the aforementioned issues are rendered hereinafter in the succeeding paragraphs.

1. Whether the deceased Manpreet Singh sustained fatal injuries in the accident which occurred on 12.03.2016 at about 09.07 PM at NH-8, Main Road Near Landing Point Mahipalpur, New Delhi caused by rash and negligent driving of vehicle No. DL-1LL-8924 being driven by respondent no. 1 and owned by respondent no. 2 ? sentences.text: Onus to prove this issue was upon the claimants.

The first question that needs to be decided is whether the accident was caused by the vehicle bearing registration No. DL-1LL-8924.
15.
The defence of the respondents is that the possibility of occurrence of accident because of slippery road cannot be ruled out.

As per the affidavit in evidence of DW1 Sh. Ankit (the helper) and DW2(R-1) Sh. Chandan (the driver) of the offending vehicle i.e. three wheeler Champion, it was raining heavily and hail storm was going on because of which they both were sitting in the vehicle.
Suddenly, one Activa scooty bearing registration no. DL 4SCL 4071 (victim's scooty), came from behind and fell down on the right side of their vehicle.
On the other hand, as per the DAR, Sh. Ankit (DW1) had informed that IO that scooty had fell in front of their vehicle and it appeared as if some vehicle had hit it.
These witnesses have avoided to say in their evidence whether at that time their vehicle was moving or was it standstill.

As per the statement of Sh. Ankit, who was also the caller,
recorded by the IO, their vehicle was standstill as it had got punctured. There is absolutely no averment as to whether they had taken proper precautions such as using reflectors or switching on tail lights while parking their vehicle on a road with moving traffic specially in the circumstances where hail storm was also going on.
16. I shall now refer to the site plan filed along with the DAR.
The direction of traffic on the road on which accident took place is North to South.
The scooty was found towards the right side of that road.
Thus, going by the evidence and averments in DAR, the offending vehicle was also parked on the right side of the road which is an improper way of parking a vehicle specially during inclement weather.
17. I shall now refer to the mechanical inspection report of the scooty which has been filed as Annexure A of the DAR.

As per this report, its front mud guard, front side body frame, head light,
head light visor and speedo meter were broken and dislocated.
Front fork of the scooty was also damaged.
Centre lower side body was broken.
Brakes were also broken.
This kind of damage is more commensurate with the scenario where the scooty dashed against the vehicle from behind than the scenario painted by the respondents.

Keeping in view the damage caused to the scooty and the above discussed testimonies of the DW1 and DW2, site plan and chargesheet, it is apparent that the accident took place because of negligent and rash parking of the offending vehicle by R-1 on the wrong side of the road without proper precautions during inclement weather conditions.
18. During the course of cross examination, DW2 (R-1) Sh. Chandan deposed that service of the vehicle was got done after one month of the accident but he could not say when it was repaired.

The possibility of the offending vehicle having been got repaired during the six months period from the date of accident till the information of the offending vehicle was received by the police from father of the deceased (on 17.09.2016) cannot be ruled out.

19. It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a Civil Court and in Civil matters, the facts are required to be established on preponderance of probabilities and not beyond reasonable doubt as are required in a criminal prosecution.

Reference in this regard is made to the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court reported as (2009) 13 SC 530 in Bimla Devi and others Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others,
Jagjeet Singh vs Chandan on 8 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62281313/
4 wherein it has been observed that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular vehicle in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants and the claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
20.

sentences.text: In view of circumstances in which the accident took place and the trauma that father of the deceased must have undergone, delay in disclosure of the offending vehicle is not fatal to the present case.
The delay has also been well explained in the chargesheet.
Claimant no. 1 informed the IO about death of his son because of injuries caused in the accident on 15.05.2016.
He was not aware that the police had to be informed about death.

On 17.09.2016, he wrote to the IO that one Ajeet had given him the registration number of the offending vehicle along with some articles of the deceased to him while the deceased was still hospitalized.
Because of trauma, he could not take phone number of that man and the registration number of the vehicle got misplaced.
As soon as he traced it out, he informed the police.

21. The discharge summary of Indian Spinal Injuries Centre from 13.03.2016 to 31.03.2016 and 31.03.2016 to 13.04.2016 mentions that the patient/deceased was a case of head injury with fracture left tibia and fibula shaft following history of RTA on 12.03.2016.
The deceased was discharged on 13.04.2016.
The deceased died on 14.04.2016.
There is, therefore, no doubt that the deceased died because of the injuries suffered in the accident.
22. As per the DAR/chargesheet, the accident took place because of the rash and negligent act of R-1/driver of the offending vehicle.

23. In cases National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pushpa Rana, 2009 ACJ 287 and United India Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Deepak Goel and Ors., 2014 (2) TAC 846 (Del.) decided by the Coordinate Bench of the Hon'ble Delhi High Court, it was held that "......where the claimants filed either the certified copies of the criminal record or the criminal record showing the completion of investigation by police or issuance of charge sheet under Section 279/304A IPC or the certified copy of FIR or the recovery of the mechanical inspection report of the offending vehicle, then these documents are sufficient proof to reach to a conclusion that the driver was negligent particularly when there is no defence available from the side of driver."
24. Reliance is being placed upon the judgment of Hon'ble Delhi High Court in case Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Meera Devi & ors., 2021 LawSuit (Del) 2021 wherein it was held that "......in view of Delhi Motor Accident Claim Tribunal Rules, 2008, contents of DAR has to be presumed to be correct and read in evidence without formal proof of the same unless proof to the contrary was produced."

In view of foregoing discussion, it stands proved by preponderance of probability that the aforesaid accident took place due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle bearing registration no. HR-39E-7459 and the said vehicle at that time was driven by respondent no. 1,
owned by respondent no. 2, insured with respondent no. 3.
Hence, this issue is decided in favour of the claimants and against the respondents.
Whether the claimants are entitled for compensation?

If so, to what amount and from whom?
28.

As rashness and negligence on part of driver of the offending vehicle/respondent No. 1 has been proved, the claimants have become entitled to be compensation for death of their family member in the said accident, but the computation of compensation and liability to pay the same are required to be decided.
(i) Loss of dependency 29.

The claimant no. 1 being father of the deceased stepped into the witness box as PW1 and filed his evidence by way of affidavit as Ex. PW1/A wherein he claimed that his deceased son, being commerce graduate, was working in a private company namely ACE CABS Pvt. Ltd., Gurugram,
Haryana and also taking tuition at home and earning more than Rs. 30,000/- per month.

PW1 has tendered on record copy of educational qualification certificate of deceased as Mark A, copy of appointment letter of deceased along with other relevant documents as Ex. PW1/7 (colly) and copy of ITRs of deceased for the assessment years 2014-15 and 2015-16 as Ex. PW1/8 (colly).
30.

Perusal of appointment letter of deceased reveals that the deceased was working on the post of Executive- Reservations, Department-Operations with ACE CABS Pvt. Ltd., Gurugram, Haryana and his CTC for the financial year 2015-16 was Rs.2,34,000/-.
31.

Perusal of income tax return for the assessment year 2015-16 which is part of Ex. PW1/8 (colly),
reveals the gross total income of deceased as Rs.2,81,922 and no income tax was deducted.

Accordingly, the monthly income of deceased comes out to be Rs. 23,494/-.
32.
In order to prove the age of deceased, PW1 has tendered on record copy of passport of deceased as Ex. PW1/3 (OSR) in which the date of birth of deceased is found recorded as 10.09.1993.

Hence,
going by this document, the age of deceased as on the date of accident i.e. on 12.03.2016 was 22 years, 6 months and 2 days.

In terms of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma & Ors. Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr., (2009) 6 SCC 121, which has also been approved by the Constitution Bench of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors., (2017) 16 SCC 680, the multiplier of '18' is applicable in the present case.

sentences.text: 33. Now coming to calculation of loss of dependency, the present claim petition has been filed by two claimants i.e. father and mother of deceased.
The deceased was unmarried at the time of accident.
Hence, in terms of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma & Ors. (Supra) and Pranay Sethi & Ors.
(Supra),

half of earnings of deceased shall be deducted Jagjeet Singh vs Chandan on 8 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62281313/
6 towards his personal and living expenses.
34. The appointment letter dated 01.03.2016 (Ex. PW1/7) shows that the deceased was employed as Executive- Reservations, Department-Operations to be based in New Delhi/NCR.
There is nothing to show that the job of the deceased was temporary in nature.
His job, therefore, shall be considered permanent in nature.
In view of the law laid down in the case of Pranay Sethi & Ors. (Supra), the claimants are held entitled to addition of 50% of earning of the deceased towards future prospects.

Thus, the loss of dependency in the claimants case comes to Rs.38,06,028/-{(Rs.23,494/-X 12 X 18 X 50/100 X 150/100)}.
(ii) COMPENSATION UNDER NON-PECUNIARY HEADS 35.

In terms of propositions of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi (Supra), the claimants are also held entitled to amount of Rs.15,000/- each under the head of loss of estate and funeral expenses, i.e. Rs.30,000/- under both heads.

3 14.
Keeping in view the damage caused to the scooty and the above discussed testimonies of the DW1 and DW2, site plan and chargesheet, it is apparent that the accident took place because of negligent and rash parking of the offending vehicle by R-1 on the wrong side of the road without proper precautions during inclement weather conditions.
The possibility of the offending vehicle having been got repaired during the six months period from the date of accident till the information of the offending vehicle was received by the police from father of the deceased (on 17.09.2016) cannot be ruled out.
19. It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a Civil Court and in Civil matters, the facts are required to be established on preponderance of probabilities and not beyond reasonable doubt as are required in a criminal prosecution.
Reference in this regard is made to the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court reported as (2009) 13 SC 530 in Bimla Devi and others Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others,
Jagjeet Singh vs Chandan on 8 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62281313/
4 wherein it has been observed that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular vehicle in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants and the claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
20.
The delay has also been well explained in the chargesheet.
Claimant no. 1 informed the IO about death of his son because of injuries caused in the accident on 15.05.2016.
He was not aware that the police had to be informed about death.
The deceased was discharged on 13.04.2016.
The deceased died on 14.04.2016.
There is, therefore, no doubt that the deceased died because of the injuries suffered in the accident.
22. As per the DAR/chargesheet, the accident took place because of the rash and negligent act of R-1/driver of the offending vehicle.
23. In cases National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pushpa Rana, 2009 ACJ 287 and United India Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Deepak Goel and Ors., 2014 (2) TAC 846 (Del.) decided by the Coordinate Bench of the Hon'ble Delhi High Court, it was held that "......where the claimants filed either the certified copies of the criminal record or the criminal record showing the completion of investigation by police or issuance of charge sheet under Section 279/304A IPC or the certified copy of FIR or the recovery of the mechanical inspection report of the offending vehicle, then these documents are sufficient proof to reach to a conclusion that the driver was negligent particularly when there is no defence available from the side of driver."
24. Reliance is being placed upon the judgment of Hon'ble Delhi High Court in case Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Meera Devi & ors., 2021 LawSuit (Del) 2021 wherein it was held that "......in view of Delhi Motor Accident Claim Tribunal Rules, 2008, contents of DAR has to be presumed to be correct and read in evidence without formal proof of the same unless proof to the contrary was produced."
25. The Hon'ble Apex Court in Mangla Ram Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. & Ors., 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303 has observed that filing of charge sheet against the driver prima facie points towards his complicity in driving the vehicle rashly and negligently.
As rashness and negligence on part of driver of the offending vehicle/respondent No. 1 has been proved, the claimants have become entitled to be compensation for death of their family member in the said accident, but the computation of compensation and liability to pay the same are required to be decided.
The claimant no. 1 being father of the deceased stepped into the witness box as PW1 and filed his evidence by way of affidavit as Ex. PW1/A wherein he claimed that his deceased son, being commerce graduate, was working in a private company namely ACE CABS Pvt. Ltd., Gurugram,
Haryana and also taking tuition at home and earning more than Rs. 30,000/- per month.
In order to prove the age of deceased, PW1 has tendered on record copy of passport of deceased as Ex. PW1/3 (OSR) in which the date of birth of deceased is found recorded as 10.09.1993.
Hence,
going by this document, the age of deceased as on the date of accident i.e. on 12.03.2016 was 22 years, 6 months and 2 days.
In terms of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma & Ors. Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr., (2009) 6 SCC 121, which has also been approved by the Constitution Bench of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors., (2017) 16 SCC 680, the multiplier of '18' is applicable in the present case.
33. Now coming to calculation of loss of dependency, the present claim petition has been filed by two claimants i.e. father and mother of deceased.
The deceased was unmarried at the time of accident.
Hence, in terms of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma & Ors. (Supra) and Pranay Sethi & Ors.
There is nothing to show that the job of the deceased was temporary in nature.
His job, therefore, shall be considered permanent in nature.
In view of the law laid down in the case of Pranay Sethi & Ors. (Supra), the claimants are held entitled to addition of 50% of earning of the deceased towards future prospects.
Out of the awarded amount, 40% share is being awarded to claimant no. 1 i.e. father of deceased and the remaining 60% share is being awarded to claimant no. 2 i.e. mother of deceased.
The disbursement to the claimants is, however, subject to addition of future interest till deposit proportionately and also deduction of proportionate tax on the interest amount or amount of interim award, if any, to/from their shares.
